title: Former German spy chief arrested for espionage and treason
content_c:
Former German spy chief arrested for espionage and treason
- Published
Former German spy chief August Hanning has been arrested on suspicion of espionage, treason and obtaining classified information for a foreign power, the German Federal Prosecutor's Office says.
Hanning headed the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) from 1998 to 2005 and has since been working as a private consultant.
Prosecutors allege that he used classified intelligence to "draft an analysis" for one foreign intelligence service and maintained contact with another foreign spying service. Investigators have not disclosed which foreign powers were involved.
Police also arrested former BND employee Manfred D, accusing him of passing Hanning about 2,000 classified documents for money.
Manfred D, who was Hanning's bureau chief and remained in the BND until this year, is charged with aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage.
Local media reported Hanning was arrested at his home in Nordwalde near Münster while Manfred D was arrested in Bavaria. Hanning is due in court on Wednesday and Manfred D will appear on Tuesday.
Prosecutors say Manfred D, who also served as the chief of staff for Hanning's successors between 2012 and 2026, used his role to gain access to highly confidential information which he then passed on to Hanning "in exchange for remuneration".
"The current findings suggest that, over the years, Manfred D provided Hanning with approximately 2,000 documents, many of which contained classified information to be used exclusively by the Federal Intelligence Service for internal purposes," the statement says.
"On one occasion, Hanning used classified intelligence ... to draft an analysis for an officer of a foreign intelligence service," prosecutors said, noting it was not clear if "the material reached the intended recipient".
Hanning is also accused of being "in close contact with a representative of another foreign intelligence service, to whom he passed on political information, partially based on material provided by Manfred D, for several years".
Local media say Hanning's alleged possession of intelligence documents came to light during a separate case relating to German steakhouse heiress Christina Block.
Hamburg public prosecutor's office accused Block of orchestrating the kidnapping of her two youngest children in 2023 due to a custody dispute. Investigators allege Hanning was involved in an earlier attempted kidnapping of the children, which he denies.
State criminal police officers reportedly discovered an electronic data storage device containing sensitive information including recent BND documents.
It is not the first time the BND has faced similar controversy. A high-ranking German intelligence officer was charged with treason in 2023 for allegedly passing state secrets to Russia.
Prosecutors alleged Carsten L shared intelligence about the war in Ukraine and the Wagner mercenary group and received roughly €400,000 ($450,000; £340,000). His trial is ongoing.
description: August Hanning is accused of obtaining classified information for a foreign power.

title: Tories pledge £10bn for British anti-missile defence system
content_c:
Tories pledge £10bn for British anti-missile defence system
- Published
The Conservatives have pledged to invest £10bn in a system to defend Britain against long-range missiles and drones, if they win the next general election.
The party said the "Britannia Shield" would offer the UK an integrated network of radar, command and control systems, as well as interceptor missiles.
The Tories initially said the system would be "in essence a British 'Iron Dome'", likening it to Israel's missile shield, however party leader Kemi Badenoch drew back from the comparison in broadcast interviews.
She said the plan would be funded from within their commitment to spend 3% of GDP on defence by 2030, paid for by welfare reform and reprioritisation of other spending.
Badenoch said that the £10bn cost would be split over 10 years, with £1bn allocated each year for the project.
Earlier this year, Gen Sir Richard Barrons told MPs on the Commons defence select committee "the cost of an iron dome at entry level is probably £80bn over 10 years".
Speaking to the BBC, Badenoch said: "We are not building the iron dome... we are designing something specific for the kind of threat that we face here."
She added: "It is not going to be the daily onslaught that Israel has, so we don't need that level of capability."
- What are Israel's Iron Dome and other missile shields? 
  - Published16 October 2024
The Conservative leader said she had been listening to figures like Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and following the impact of the war in Iran on Gulf countries when crafting her plans.
"There is a new type of warfare," she said, adding: "Drone warfare requires a different type of missile defence.
"We could have a situation for example where people could come in very close to the English Channel and are able to send drones and missiles at our critical national infrastructure."
Pressed on how her party would fund the spending, Badenoch said: "We are not messing around - we are very very concerned about the state not just of our defence but the state of our economy.
"We need to get serious, we need to find savings."
She said the Conservatives would find savings from the welfare budget, redirecting spending on net-zero research, reinstating the two-child benefit cap and restricting housing benefits.
"Some people may not agree with those decisions but we are making choices."
The Tories added the proposal would strengthen the UK's air defence systems at a time when Nato allies have warned they are facing repeated Russian drone incursions.
The party also cited a report from the defence committee of MPs last November which said the UK was lagging behind its European counterparts in having a plan to defend itself and overseas territories from a military attack.
The Conservatives said the system would have three components - new advanced radar systems, upgraded command and control systems to integrate information from across Britain's defences and rapidly decide a response, and new interceptor missiles as well as counter-drone capabilities.
The three-tiered design of the proposal is similar to the British Army's current Sky Sabre, external air defence system.
This system - which can intercept munitions and aircraft as well as integrate with wider air defences - was deployed by the UK to the Middle East earlier this year for defensive action against Iranian attacks.
Sidharth Kaushal, a senior fellow at the defence and security think tank RUSI (the Royal United Services Institute), said £10bn would "probably cover" what the UK "actually needs" including horizon radar and more E-7 aircraft.
"In contrast, if what the Conservatives envision is a truly Israeli-style multi-layered missile defence system, £10bn probably wouldn't get there," he said.
"But that system would also be quite superfluous, arguably."
Prof Steven Barrett, CEO of Cambridge Aerospace which has been developing interceptor missiles, told the BBC £10bn was a "significant commitment" but the exact cost of the project would depend on the detail of the Conservatives' proposal.
He said that it would not be practical for the system to defend "every square inch" of UK territory and a more plausible setup would cover "significant parts of the population in key high density areas".
He also said there needed to be a focus on protecting critical national infrastructure, adding that a "huge amount of damage" could be done if data centres used by transport and health systems came under attack.
In his speech at the conference in Birmingham, shadow defence secretary James Cartlidge said: "With a £10bn budget, this would be one of Britain's most significant military programmes since the Cold War.
"But one that is totally necessary because of the threats we face."
Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said in response: "They [the Conservatives] cut the Army to its smallest size since Napoleon and left a £17bn hole in the equipment plan.
"Their own defence secretary, Ben Wallace, admitted our Armed Forces had been 'hollowed out and underfunded'."
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has been under pressure to set out how he will reach Nato's 3.5% of GDP spending target by 2035, up from an estimated 2.6% this year.
The current Labour government's Defence Investment Plan includes more than £350m to double the number of Sky Sabre systems operated by the British Army, with ground-based air defence sitting alongside air and maritime capabilities.
Sign up for our Politics Essential newsletter to keep up with the inner workings of Westminster and beyond.
description: The Conservatives say their plan would protect the UK at a time when Nato allies have warned of Russian drone incursions.

title: Froyo's made a comeback. But at £12 a tub will it last?
content_c:
Froyo's made a comeback. But at £12 a tub will it last?
- Published
Kiersten Paterno was one of the many people willing to queue up to an hour to treat herself to some frozen yoghurt.
"It was a 45-minute wait for my turn but the whole experience of choosing your flavours and customising it with different toppings was a big part of the appeal for me," the 19-year-old student says.
Froyo was a huge trend in the UK in the late 2000s and early 2010s and was most popular in London.
Chains like Snog had 10 stores in the capital at its peak and other brands like AngelBerry had shops in Bristol and Brighton.
And this year it's made a comeback, driven by nostalgia, social media and its perception as a healthier dessert choice.
Several brands such as Go Greek, Myka and Yo-Chi launched in London, while Frurt, which operates mainly in the north west of England and Yorkshire, has opened new stores, including one in Leicester.
These companies saw hundreds of customers queueing to create their own dessert pot, despite it not being a particularly cheap treat, with tubs costing as much as £12.
Kiersten says she was initially attracted to the dessert as she could manage portion size and sweetness level.
"I could control how sweet I wanted it to be through the toppings. It feels healthier overall as it's a dessert I can enjoy without feeling like I've overindulged."
She admits it can be pricey but says she doesn't mind spending a little more as an occasional treat.
Sweet treat culture
Research suggests the froyo market is steadily growing. Market Data Forecast estimates that the European frozen yoghurt market is worth £434m in 2026, up from £419m last year.
Australian brand Yo-Chi opened a Notting Hill branch in August and blew up quickly on social media for its range of toppings and "third space" feel.
"Sweet treat culture is huge. People aren't spending a fortune on big things, but a little thing like that, they're happy to," says Bethan Clarke, Yo-Chi campaign manager.
While Yo-Chi would "never call ourselves healthy" - froyo is usually lower in calories and fat than ice cream, but may also contain more added sugar - Clarke says the fact that it is customisable means that people are in control of their own portion sizes and sugar levels.
Social media trends like "2026 is the new 2016" are helping froyo's virality.
"People are coming back to re-experience childhood a little bit," says Clarke.
Ella Light, who also works for Yo-Chi, says she's been surprised by the mix of people coming into the store.
"I was kind of expecting to see the Gen Z girlies coming in, [but] this morning there was a group of builders!"
2010s throwbacks with a modern twist
But how likely is the current froyo craze to survive? After all, it was huge in the 2010s but by the end of that decade was all but dead.
Vhari Russell, founder of Food Marketing Experts, says: "Market over-saturation played a role in the initial disappearance of froyo, as well as the natural cycle of dying trends."
Market leader Snog faced increasing competition from the likes of Yog, Yoomoo and Pinkberry, while consumers also realised that the dessert may not have been the healthier option they initially thought it was.
"But now 2010s throwbacks coupled with a modern twist are seeing huge appetite across the market," says Russell.
Will £12 for a tub eventually start to put people off though?
Russell doesn't believe so, as she calls it an "affordable luxury".
Going out for a froyo can be "an experiential moment" as much as anything, she adds.
"For many people, they don't smoke or have expensive lifestyles, so froyo isn't viewed as food, it's viewed as an experience."
Not interested in queuing for two hours? Here's how to make your own
If the price of froyo seems unreasonable or if you can’t justify queueing for hours, BBC Food have five different froyo variations you can make at home.
description: Frozen yoghurt, which was a huge craze in the 2000s and 2010s, has made its return with multiple chains popping up across the wider UK.

title: US man arrested as second suspect in Canada mass school shooting planned with ChatGPT
content_c:
A surprise suspected accomplice has been arrested in connection with a mass school shooting in Canada that was made notorious after an 18-year-old allegedly killed six children after discussing it with the AI chatbot ChatGPT.
The US Department of Justice said Tuesday it had detained James Codey Bryant, 30, a resident of western Washington state, on a charge of conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country.
Bryant offered money and “technical advice” to the suspected shooter for six months leading up to the killings, the justice department alleged.
Canadian police have identified the suspect in this year’s massacre of eight people – including her mother and half-brother, as well as the six children, making it the second-deadliest school shooting in the country’s history – as Jesse Van Rootselaar, who has a history of mental health problems.
It had been known that Van Rootselaar had used ChatGPT to plan the attack, which took place in February. The safety team at OpenAI, the company that owns the chatbot, flagged Van Rootselaar internally after she conducted conversations with it about gun violence, but the company did not alert police. It did reportedly close Van Rootselaar’s account, but she started a second one that was not closed. Victims’ families and the province of British Columbia have sued OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, for failing to report her behaviour.
It was not previously known publicly that Van Rootselaar was also talking to a human about her plans.
In a joint press conference with the justice department and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) on Tuesday, authorities alleged that Bryant and Van Rootselaar met on the now-defunct messaging service Omegle about three years prior to the shooting and kept in contact.
Neil Floyd, acting US attorney, and W Mike Herrington, the special agent in charge for the FBI’s Seattle bureau, said they believe Bryant sent Van Rootselaar about $100 to buy new shoes and aabout $15 for a lighter.
Authorities said there is no indication so far that the two suspects ever met in person.
According to an indictment obtained by CBC, Bryant was “knowingly and wilfully” conspiring with Van Rootselaar beginning in or before August 2025.
That August, Bryant told Van Rootselaar the pair should “find a way to delete” their messages, and in mid-December Bryant suggested getting a VPN to avoid detection for “posting a shooting video online”, according to the court document reviewed by CBC.
Police said that on several occasions Bryant tried to talk Van Rootselaar out of committing the attack, but did not contact law enforcement.
They added that after Van Rootselaar shot and killed her mother and brother in their family home, she was unable to start the car. Bryant advised her on how to turn on the engine, thereby allowing the shooter to reach the school and execute the attack, authorities said.
Bryant also allegedly agreed to livestream the mass shooting, which Harrington said police were not sure Van Rootselaar would have committed had Bryant not done so.
It was not clear whether the suspect was represented by a lawyer. Bryant will be prosecuted in the US as a US citizen under an investigation by the FBI, which said it will continue working closely with Canadian authorities.
author: Keely Aouga

title: The Guardian view on the Green party and Palestine: rejecting two states is no shortcut to peace | Editorial
content_c:
Last year, the UN general assembly endorsed the New York Declaration supporting two states in the Holy Land by 142 votes to 10. Those voting against included the US and Israel. The wider international diplomatic consensus rests on a 2002 UN security council resolution, which explicitly affirmed a two-state vision for Israel and Palestine. Saudi Arabia’s then crown prince said peace required “two equal parties” and could not survive “oppression and humiliation”. His words remain as relevant now as then.
The Green party has now rejected that two-state framework in favour of a one-state solution. The Guardian strongly disagrees with this move. Peace needs to acknowledge reality: the latest polls in Gaza and the West Bank suggest that a majority support a two-state formula based on the 1967 borders compared with just 10% who back a single democratic state with equal rights. The European Greens also disagree with the new direction of their English and Welsh sister party. The EU-wide representatives argue that the policy is incompatible with previously agreed positions. Europe’s Greens – which include the centrist German party – condemn “the genocide against Palestinians” and call for sanctions against Israel’s government.
Political scientists say that currently, west of the Jordan River, one system under Israeli control enforces unequal laws and relegates Palestinians to a “lower caste”. The international consensus has plainly failed to deliver Palestinian statehood, or indeed prevent the near-total destruction of Gaza by Israel. But a “single democratic” entity in Palestine seems even more remote. There may need to be fresh future thinking about peace, including confederation models being considered as the crisis deepens in the occupied Palestinian territories. The ultimate test of any solution to the Israel-Palestine conflict is whether it ends domination by any one group and provides equal rights so both peoples have a secure political future.
The vote at the Green party conference to adopt a controversial set of policies was decided by about 200 votes – less than one-thousandth of the membership. The Greens’ leader, Zack Polanski, who is himself Jewish, has become embroiled in a row over antisemitism around the third anniversary of the 7 October attacks, at a time when he is fighting a parliamentary byelection in London. The motion defines Zionism as being “to the exclusion and/or domination of the non-Jewish population” in historic Palestine. Most in the Jewish community disagree, seeing it solely in terms of Jewish self-determination. The anger is real and understandable. There could be real-world consequences. The policy declares that an ideology that most Jewish people identify with is racist and raises the question of whether someone who identifies as a Zionist can remain in the Greens.
Green delegates rejected safeguards against disciplining members for affiliation with Jewish institutions identifying as Zionist. Lawyers warn that Zionist beliefs may qualify for protection under equality legislation. On Monday, Mr Polanski ruled out “exclusion, or refusal to engage with anyone” in the Greens because of religious or communal affiliation. The test is whether the party honours this in practice. Whatever the motion’s eventual impact, it is clear that Green party structures urgently need to be reformed for a mass membership base. Mr Polanski, a London assembly member, wants to join the five Green MPs in parliament. He will need to show a surer political touch to get there.

title: French AI company announces new, private model
content_c:
Mistral: French firm announces Le Chonk, a private AI model
October 6, 2026
Frenchtech company Mistral on Tuesday announced the upcoming release of "Le Chonk," its biggest AIopen-weight model, aimed at users wanting to keep their data private.
Popular AI models from companies like Anthropic and OpenAIrely on closed models.
Le Chonk, officially named Mistral Large 4, will be made publicly available on October 27, with cybersecurity experts and government authorities receiving access to a version of the model with fewer safety restrictions to test its capabilities.
Last month, Mistral raised €3 billion euros ($3.4 billion), Europe's biggest technology fundraising.
The new AI model allows users to download and customize "weights" that determine how it computes on their own servers.
An open-weight model means a user can download the software and run it on their own hardware. While the top US models run on their own models, many of their Chinesecompetitors are open-weight.
Europe's AI hope
Mistral, considered Europe's leading AI company, said the new model outperforms many rival open-weight models.
Le Chonk is the three-year-old company's first new model release since May.
According to Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch, the new model is "actually above the Chinese models" in certain areas, including cyber.
"The narrative that Europe cannot compete is something that is not true," Mensch said at the company's event in Abu Dhabi, without specifying which Chinese models he was referring to.
MIstral has positioned itself as a safer European alternative in comparison to its main US competitors, especially given the latter companies' recent warnings regarding AI's dangers.
Edited by: Sean Sinico

title: Cristiano Ronaldo erklärt Abreise und erhebt Vorwürfe gegen Coach Jorge Jesus
content_c:
Drama um portugiesischen Nationalspieler Ronaldo wirft Trainer »Wortbruch« vor – will aber weiterspielen
Das Drama um Cristiano Ronaldo und die portugiesische Fußballnationalmannschaft geht weiter. Der Superstar hat sein Schweigen gebrochen und sorgt mit einer langen Erklärung zum Eklat um seine Abreise aus dem Quartier der portugiesischen Nationalmannschaft für weiteren Zündstoff (mehr zu dem Fall hier). Unter anderem wirft er Nationaltrainer Jorge Jesus Wortbruch vor.
Gleichzeitig bot Ronaldo aber auch die Fortsetzung seiner Länderspielkarriere an. »Ich beschloss, das Trainingslager zu verlassen, ohne auf einen weiteren Wortbruch zu warten. Für mich ist die Wahrheit nach wie vor das Wichtigste in der Beziehung zwischen Menschen«, schrieb er und erläuterte die Geschehnisse rund um seine abrupte Abreise in der vergangenen Woche.
Zugleich entschuldigte sich der 41-Jährige dafür, dass er das Team verlassen habe. »Trotz des absoluten Vertrauensbruchs seitens des Trainers – was Zeugen dieser Gespräche bestätigen können – hätte ich das nicht tun dürfen. Die Verantwortung liegt allein bei mir«, so Ronaldo. »Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass mein Verbleib von diesem Moment an der Mannschaft nur geschadet hätte, und ich tat das, was ich immer gesagt hatte: Wenn ich mich nicht mehr als nützlich empfinde, packe ich meine Sachen und gehe.«
Cristiano Ronaldo und Trainer Jorge Jesus (am 24. September)
Foto: Jose Sena Goulao / EPA
Ronaldo rechnet mit einer Sanktion vonseiten des portugiesischen Verbandes für sein Verhalten. Danach stehe er aber wieder bei Bedarf bereit. »Sollte ich also körperlich fit sein und für meinen Verein spielen – und hoffentlich auch Tore erzielen –, werde ich nach Ablauf einer eventuell gegen mich verhängten Sperre zur Verfügung stehen, um für unsere Nationalmannschaft anzutreten und zu gewinnen; so wie ich es bis heute immer getan habe.«
Ronaldo hatte die Nationalmannschaft in der vergangenen Woche verlassen, nachdem er beim 2:1 im Hinspiel in Norwegen nicht eingesetzt worden war. Ursprünglich sei ein Einsatz – genauso wie im dritten Spiel – nicht vorgesehen gewesen. Der Coach habe ihn aber vor der Partie gebeten, 30 Minuten zu spielen, wozu es nicht kam.
Nach einem klärenden Gespräch mit Jesus und Sportdirektor Simao Coutinho sollte der Coach auf der Pressekonferenz eigentlich die Angelegenheit bereinigen, so Ronaldo. »Das Auftreten hatte nichts mit unserem Treffen zu tun. Ich hörte Äußerungen und erlebte eine Aggressivität, die ich meiner Meinung nach nicht verdient hatte – eine hochmütige und arrogante Haltung, die er mir gegenüber am Vortag nicht einmal ansatzweise gezeigt hatte.«
Trainer lässt die Tür für Rückkehr offen
Nationaltrainer Jesus hatte sich nach der Abreise seines Kapitäns offen für dessen Rückkehr gezeigt (mehr hier). »Für mich ist Cris bei der nächsten Nominierung – sofern er bei al-Nassr spielt – ein Kandidat für den Kader. Wenn er zurückkehren will, wird er zurückkehren.« Zugleich sprach der 72 Jahre alte Coach, der Ronaldo in der vorigen Saison bei al-Nassr in Saudi-Arabien trainiert und den Club zur Meisterschaft geführt hatte, von einem Missverständnis, das leicht zu klären sei.
Bislang bestritt der 41-jährige Ronaldo für Portugal 234 Länderspiele, in denen er 146 Tore erzielte – beides Rekordmarken im internationalen Fußball. Nach der WM in den USA, Mexiko und Kanada hatte er bereits das Ende seiner Nationalteamkarriere ins Auge gefasst. »Nach Abschluss des Turniers, noch auf dem Rückflug aus den USA, bat mich der Präsident des Verbandes nachdrücklich, meine Entscheidung zum Abschied zu überdenken, da die FPF wollte, dass ich weitermache«, betonte Ronaldo.
Auch sei er bei der Suche nach dem neuen Nationaltrainer um eine Meinung zu Jorge Jesus gebeten worden. »Ich teilte dem Verbandspräsidenten mit, dass dies meiner Meinung nach die richtige Wahl wäre«, schrieb Ronaldo.
Titelverteidiger Portugal gewann alle vier Nations-League-Spiele in den beiden turbulenten Wochen und steht vorzeitig im Viertelfinale.
Ronaldo – die Selbstdemontage: Jahre des sportlichen Verfalls und der Sturheit kulminieren im Zerwürfnis zwischen Portugal und seinem größten Sohn. Gab es einen Verrat? Mehr dazu hier .
author: DER SPIEGEL
description: Seine Abreise von der Nationalmannschaft brachte den Eklat – nun erklärt sich Fußballidol Cristiano Ronaldo. Was er über Portugals Coach Jorge Jesus zu sagen hat, dürfte die Lage aber kaum entschärfen.

title: Vorsitz des Parlamentarischen Kontrollgremiums Henrichmann im Interview
content_c:
Spionage-Vorwurf gegen Ex-BND-Chef "Das geht in den Bereich des Landesverrates"
Die Spionage-Vorwürfe gegen Ex-BND-Chef Hanning haben "an den Grundfesten gerüttelt", sagte der Vorsitzende des Parlamentarischen Kontrollgremiums, Henrichmann, im tagesthemen-Interview. Das Wichtigste sei nun eine lückenlose Aufklärung.
tagesthemen: Wie groß ist aus Ihrer Sicht der Schaden für den deutschen Auslandsnachrichtendienst BND?
Marc Henrichmann: Er hat an den Grundfesten gerüttelt, weil sich das wahrscheinlich auch niemand hätte vorstellen können. Das geht in den Bereich des Landesverrates, wenn sich die Vorwürfe erhärten, und das bei einem hochrangigen Funktionsträger, der jetzt 20 Jahre lang nicht mehr im Amt ist.
Aber trotzdem muss das mit Blick auf die Zukunft jetzt wirklich heißen: aufklären und keinen Stein auf dem anderen lassen.
tagesthemen: Ja, denn vor einigen Jahren hatten wir den Fall Carsten L. - ein hochrangiger BND-Mitarbeiter, der für Russland spioniert haben soll. Jetzt dieser Fall. Welches Signal sendet das an unsere Partnergeheimdienste?
Henrichmann: Unsere Partner sind genauso professionell wie der BND. Man muss ja wissen, dass Herr Hanning auch wirtschaftlich schwer angeschlagen war und offenbar auch Geld benötigte nach einer Insolvenz. Unsere Partner wissen genauso, dass das anfällig macht und gegnerische Dienste immer versuchen, auf der Gegenseite Menschen in ihren Bann zu ziehen.
Wie weit das hier geht, das klärt gerade der Generalbundesanwalt. Aber der neue Präsident hat, glaube ich, ein super hohes Renommee. Die Vorgänge liegen vier Jahre zurück. Insofern ist es jetzt ein Neustart, aber der muss auch glaubwürdig sein.
tagesthemen: Aber die Frage bleibt ja: Wie sollen denn ausländische Partnerdienste vertrauensvoll zusammenarbeiten mit dem BND, wenn das Gefühl ist: Ob das nicht irgendwo anders landet, das können wir nicht sicherstellen?
Henrichmann: Das ist beim Austausch von Informationen am Ende immer ein Restrisiko - in jedem Unternehmen wie auch in jeder Sicherheitsbehörde. Das bleibt auch nie zu 100 Prozent auszuschließen. Das wissen auch unsere Partner. Und so, wie ich das wahrnehme, ist das Renommee der deutschen Dienste da auch sehr, sehr gut in der Welt.
Aber man muss jetzt auch zeigen, dass man aufklären will, dass man um Vertrauen wirbt und in einer engen Zusammenarbeit diese Lücken schließt, die gegebenenfalls auch diese Anfälligkeit ausmachen, und sie früher erkennt.
tagesthemen: Hinzu kommt aber auch, dass das Ganze ja nicht der BND selbst aufgedeckt hat, sondern die Polizei, und das auch nur per Zufall. Wie konnte das jahrelang unentdeckt bleiben?
Henrichmann: Wie gesagt, die Vorgänge werden jetzt lückenlos aufgeklärt werden müssen. Es ist auch gut, dass ohne Ansehung von Person oder Amt heute schnell gehandelt wurde und öffentlich gemacht wurde, um welche Vorwürfe es da geht. Man hat hier auch niemanden geschont. Trotzdem geht es jetzt darum, den Willen zu zeigen, da Transparenz reinzubringen.
Wir werden uns jetzt auch die Frage anschauen müssen: Was machen Funktionsträger nach ihrer aktiven Zeit? Da hat es vor einigen Jahren mal Verschärfungen gegeben. Reicht das, ist die Frage. Ich persönlich glaube mittlerweile auch eher nein. Aber wir haben auch aus dem Drohnenvorfall in Leipzig gelernt, dass es Sinn macht, die Ermittlungen jetzt erst mal abzuwarten. Was ist konkret überhaupt passiert? Welche Unterlagen sind herausgegeben worden?
Es gilt auch im BND ja immer das "Need-to-know-Prinzip": Jeder weiß das, was er eigentlich wissen muss. Und insofern stellt sich die Frage: Wie brisant war das? Wir reden jetzt über Dossiers, die Herr Hanning erstellt haben soll, also nicht über brühwarme Informationen. Wer weiß, wie groß das noch wird? Die Arbeit fängt jetzt an.
tagesthemen: Wie sehr, glauben Sie, bedroht oder zumindest beeinflusst dieser Fall jetzt die geplante Ausweitung der Befugnisse des BND? Wir haben ja gestern bei der öffentlichen Anhörung gehört, wie ernst die allgemeine Lage ist und dass es neue Befugnisse für den Bundesnachrichtendienst geben soll.
Henrichmann: Ich glaube, wir haben in Deutschland jetzt zwei Wege, die wir theoretisch gehen. Der eine, den ich für falsch halte, ist jetzt zu sagen: "Unsere Dienste müssen wieder ganz eng an die Kette gelegt werden und mit hoher Bürokratie überzogen werden."
Die Tatsache, dass so Menschen wie Herr Hanning offenbar von fremden Mächten gewonnen werden, zeigt ja, dass wir von außen ständig attackiert werden und dass man gerade auch versucht, Menschen in den sensiblen Bereichen unserer Infrastruktur, unserer Sicherheitsbehörden zu platzieren.
Deswegen ist der zweite Weg, glaube ich, genau richtig, operative Befugnisse zu erteilen, aber dann auch gleichzeitig die Kontrolle parlamentarisch und juristisch zu stärken.
tagesthemen: Sagt der Vorsitzende des Parlamentarischen Kontrollgremiums, Herr Henrichmann. Ich danke Ihnen für das Gespräch.
Das Gespräch führte Ingo Zamperoni für die tagesthemen. Es wurde für die schriftliche Fassung angepasst.
description: Die Spionage-Vorwürfe gegen Ex-BND-Chef Hanning haben "an den Grundfesten gerüttelt", so der Vorsitzende des Parlamentarischen Kontrollgremiums, Henrichmann, im tagesthemen-Interview. Das Wichtigste sei nun eine lückenlose Aufklärung.

title: Spionageverdacht gegen August Hanning: Ehemaliger Chef des Bundesnachrichtendienstes festgenommen
content_c:
Schwere Vorwürfe: Spionierte Ex-BND-Chef für anderes Land?
6. Oktober 2026
Wenn sich der Verdacht bestätigt, wäre es ein Spionagefall historischen Ausmaßes für Deutschland. Denn kein Geringerer als der frühere Chef des Bundesnachrichtendienstes (BND) ist festgenommen worden. Ihm wirft die Bundesanwaltschaft landesverräterische Ausspähung, versuchten Landesverrat und geheimdienstliche Agententätigkeit vor.
Der heute 80 Jahre alte August Hanning leitete den BND von 1998 bis 2005. Schon davor hatte er eine steile Karriere im Sicherheitsapparat hingelegt. Nach seinem Ausscheiden war er Staatssekretär im Bundesinnenministerium, wechselte anschließend in die Privatwirtschaft und arbeitete als Sicherheitsberater.
Sein Informant, so der Vorwurf der Bundesanwaltschaft, war sein ehemaliger Büroleiter Manfred D., der seine Funktion später auch unter Hannings Nachfolgern von März 2012 bis März 2026 innehatte. D. hatte damit Zugriff auf zahlreiche geheime Informationen.
Geheiminformationen aus dem Kanzleramt
Manfred D. soll über Jahre fast 2000 teilweise hochsensible BND-Unterlagen gegen Geld an Hanning weitergegeben haben. Die Dokumente soll Hanning dann für seine private Beratertätigkeit genutzt haben.
Der schwerste Vorwurf: Hanning soll über Jahre einen engen Austausch mit dem Mitarbeiter eines ausländischen Nachrichtendienstes gehabt und ihm solche Geheiminformationen zugespielt haben. Um welches Land es ging, ist nicht bekannt. Es soll sich aber nicht um Russland handeln, heißt es nach Recherchen von WDR, NDR und Süddeutscher Zeitung.
Die Ermittler sprechen außerdem von einer Analyse, die Hanning für einen Mitarbeiter eines weiteren fremden Geheimdienstes erstellt haben soll. Es sei aber nicht sicher, ob die Analyse diesen erreicht habe.
Bei den Geheiminformationen ging es auch um die routinemäßigen Treffen der Chefs der deutschen Sicherheitsbehörden im Kanzleramt. Themen waren unter anderem das iranische Atomprogramm und Analysen zu den russischen Streitkräften.
Da dabei auch Erkenntnisse ausländischer Partnerdienste weitergegeben worden sein sollen, könnte das auch deren Vertrauen in den deutschen BND erschüttern und dazu führen, dass künftig die nachrichtendienstliche Zusammenarbeit mit Deutschland erschwert wird.
Hanning geriet in Zusammenhang mit Entführungsfall ins Visier
"Ein guter Agent zeichnet sich dadurch aus, dass er nicht auffällt", sagte August Hanning einmal. Jetzt fiel er selbst auf, allerdings zunächst in ganz anderem Zusammenhang.
Denn im September 2025 durchsuchte das Hamburger Landeskriminalamt Hannings Haus und Büros im Entführungsfall Block. Christina Block ist Erbin der "Steak-House"-Restaurantkette. Die Hamburger Staatsanwaltschaft wirft ihr vor, Ende 2023 wegen eines Sorgerechtsstreits die Entführung ihrer beiden jüngsten Kinder in Auftrag gegeben zu haben.
Gut ein Jahr vor der Rückholaktion der Kinder aus dem Ausland soll es bereits einen gescheiterten Entführungsversuch gegeben haben. Es gab damals den Verdacht, dass Hanning daran beteiligt war, was dieser bestreitet.
Bei der Durchsuchung 2025 fanden die Ermittler einen elektronischen Datenträger mit streng geheimen BND-Dokumenten aus jüngerer Zeit. Das Landeskriminalamt übergab die Unterlagen der Bundesanwaltschaft. Im Mai 2026 leitete sie zunächst verdeckte Ermittlungen gegen Hanning und Manfred D. ein. Jetzt erfolgte die Festnahme der beiden. Die jüngsten bislang gefundenen Dokumente sollen aus dem Juni 2022 stammen.
Grüne fordern Konsequenzen
Der BND hat in seiner Geschichte einige teils spektakuläre Spionagefälle gesehen. Heinz Felfe leitete in den 1960er Jahren das Referat "Gegenspionage Sowjetunion" und arbeitete zugleich für den sowjetischen Geheimdienst KGB. 2014 flog ein BND-Mitarbeiter als Spion für den amerikanischen CIA auf.
Der Prozess um den Geheimnisverrat eines BND-Mannes an Russlands FSB im September und Oktober 2022, also nach Beginn des Ukraine-Krieges, dauert an. Doch noch nie stand bei Spionageverdacht ein ehemaliger Beamter vom Range eines August Hanning im Fokus.
"Der BND hat frühzeitig und unverzüglich umfangreiche interne Ermittlungen einleiten lassen, die den Verdacht erhärteten", teilte der heutige BND-Präsident Martin Jäger mit. "Für den BND und mich gibt es bei der internen Sicherheit keine Kompromisse."
Doch von politischer Seite gibt es teils heftige Kritik. Günter Krings von der konservativen Regierungspartei CDU sagte der "Rheinischen Post": "Alleine der Verdacht, dass ein ehemaliger BND-Chef Geheimnisse verkauft, ist schädlich für das Vertrauen in unsere Sicherheitsbehörden."
Konstantin von Notz, Grünen-Politiker und Vizechef des Parlamentarischen Kontrollgremiums, das die Nachrichtendienste überwacht, sagt: "Es sind schlimme und abgründige Vorwürfe, die gegen August Hanning im Raum stehen." Er fordert im Namen seiner Partei, Lobby-Tätigkeiten ehemaliger Spitzenbeamter und höchster Geheimnisträger stärker in den Blick zu nehmen. "Diese sind offenkundig auch ein Einfallstor für gegnerische Geheimdienste", analysiert von Notz. Er fordert: Die Bundesregierung müsse diese "illegitimen Praktiken" sofort unterbinden.
Noch weiter geht Clara Bünger, innenpolitische Sprecherin der Linksfraktion im Bundestag: "Die Ermittlungen gegen den Ex-BND-Chef Hanning zeigen erneut: Die Geheimdienste sind selbst ein Sicherheitsrisiko."
Allerdings ist wichtig zu betonen, dass die Vorwürfe gegen August Hanning und Manfred D. bisher nur ein Verdacht sind. Ob sie zutreffen, wird ein Gericht zu beurteilen haben.
description: Noch ist es nur ein Verdacht. Aber ausgerechnet dem früheren Leiter des deutschen Auslandsgeheimdienst wird Agententätigkeit für das Ausland vorgeworfen.

title: Letztes Spiel in Nationalelf: Große Emotionen bei «Messis letztem Tango» für Argentinien
content_c:
Lionel Messi ist vor seinem letzten Spiel für die argentinische Nationalmannschaft frenetisch gefeiert worden. Fangesänge, grenzenloser Jubel und ein Feuerwerk bildeten die Ouvertüre für einen historischen Fußball-Abend im ausverkauften Monumental-Stadion von Buenos Aires: für «Messis letzten Tango», bei dem das Freundschaftsspiel gegen Benin den Rahmen bot.
Es war ein besonderer Moment der Fußball-Historie. Keiner hat den Weltfußball in den letzten zwei Jahrzehnten so konstant und nachhaltig geprägt wie Messi. Mit seinem letzten Länderspiel tritt der Superstar, der auf Vereinsebene noch bei Inter Miami spielt, nun von der großen Fußballbühne ab.
«Gracias» in goldenen Lettern
Ohrenbetäubend war der Jubel, als die Stadionsprecherin in dem 85.000 Zuschauer fassenden Rund vor dem Spiel «ein letztes Mal» den Namen des Superstars aufrief. Ein riesengroßes himmelblau-weißes Trikot wurde über den Rasen gespannt, auf dem Messis Nummer 10 sowie ein «Gracias» («Danke») in großen goldenen Lettern aufgedruckt war.
Bereits vor dem Spiel hatte Messi in einem auf Instagram verbreiteten Video mitgeteilt: «Der Moment ist gekommen. (...) Dieses Trikot war mein Traum, mein Stolz und mein Leben. Danke, dass ihr mich so sehr geliebt habt, ich werde euch vermissen.»
Die Partie gegen Benin ist der Schlusspunkt einer über 21-jährigen Länderspiel-Karriere, die am 17. August 2005 gegen Ungarn sehr holprig begonnen hatte. Denn bei seinem Debüt handelte sich der eingewechselte Messi in weniger als einer Minute eine Rote Karte ein, die ihm der deutsche Schiedsrichter Markus Merk wegen einer Tätlichkeit zeigte.
Messi brauchte tatsächlich einen langen Anlauf, um in der Nationalmannschaft die ganz großen Erfolge zu erzielen und sich in die Herzen seiner Landsleute zu spielen. Der Gewinn der Copa América im Jahr 2021 war der erste wichtige Titel, den Messi mit der «Albiceleste» feiern konnte. Absoluter Höhepunkt war der WM-Triumph 2022 in Katar. Ein weiterer Erfolg bei der Copa América (2024) sowie zwei Vizeweltmeisterschaften (2014 und 2026) runden Messis beeindruckende Laufbahn in der Nationalmannschaft ab, deren Rekordspieler (208 Spiele) und Rekordtorschütze (125 Tore, vor Benin-Spiel) er ist.

title: Китайський ШІ-агент допоміг хакерам зламати сім найбільших банків Південної Кореї
content_c:
Китайський ШІ-агент допоміг хакерам зламати сім найбільших банків Південної Кореї
Хакери використали китайського агента штучного інтелекту для атаки на найбільші банки Південної Кореї та викрадення особистих даних 68 тисяч осіб.
Джерело: The Wall Street Journal
Деталі: За даними слідчих із Сеула, кібератаки вразили щонайменше сім південнокорейських фінансових компаній. У зламаних системах виявили сліди розробленого в Китаї інструменту кібербезпеки Artex AI.
Зловмисники викрали дані співробітників та клієнтів банків, серед яких інформація про річний дохід та ліміти за кредитами.
Artex – наступальний ШІ-агент, розроблений китайським інженером Лі Пухуа. До нього можна підключати моделі ШІ від OpenAI, Anthropic або DeepSeek. Агент самостійно виявляє вразливості та планує атаки без значного втручання людини.
Підрозділ із боротьби з кібертероризмом Національного агентства поліції вже розпочав розслідування. Правоохоронці прагнуть залучити міжнародних партнерів, оскільки атаки здійснювалися з понад 20 IP-адрес у десятках країн, зокрема у США, Японії та Німеччині.
Експерти з кібербезпеки наголошують, що подібні інциденти доводять вразливість захищених систем перед загальнодоступними інструментами штучного інтелекту.
Що передувало:
- У листопаді 2025 року американська компанія Anthropic повідомила, що китайські хакери використали її ШІ-технологію для автоматизації кібератак. Тоді зловмисники успішно атакували близько 30 цілей по всьому світу, серед яких були іноземні уряди та корпорації.
- У червні 2026 року автономний агент від OpenAI зламав урядовий портал статистики охорони здоров'я Австралії Medicare, отримавши доступ до закритих баз даних. Про цей інцидент австралійська влада офіційно повідомила лише у вересні 2026 року.
- У серпні російськомовні хакери використали ШІ-асистента для програмування Cursor від компанії SpaceX, щоб зламати бельгійську хімічну компанію та ще щонайменше шість інших фірм у Європі та США.
- У вересні модель Gemini від Google також самостійно вийшла в інтернет і здійснила хакерські атаки на інші компанії під час тестування її можливостей у сфері кібербезпеки.
author: Іван Д'яконов
description: Хакери використали китайського агента штучного інтелекту для атаки на найбільші банки Південної Кореї та викрадення особистих даних 68 тисяч осіб.

title: Депутати "засипали" бюджет рекордною кількістю правок. Дві третини – "спам"
content_c:
Депутати "засипали" бюджет рекордною кількістю правок. Дві третини – "спам"
Народні депутати подали 5236 поправок до проєкту держбюджету на 2027 рік, що найбільше щонайменше за 24 роки, однак дві третини з них голова бюджетного комітету Роксолана Підласа називає "законодавчим спамом".
Про це вона повідомила у Facebook.
За словами Підласої, кількість поправок приблизно в півтора раза перевищує торішню. Статистику ведуть із підготовки бюджету на 2003 рік.
Депутатка стверджує, що "спам" подають, аби годинами виступати в сесійній залі або домагатися врахування бажаних поправок.
За її розрахунком, якщо витрачати хоча б 90 секунд на кожну правку, розгляд усіх пропозицій займе понад 16 повних робочих днів.

Кабінет міністрів схвалив проєкт Державного бюджету на 2027 рік, його передали на розгляд Верховній Раді.

title: Росіяни просунулися біля Білицького на Донеччині — DeepState
content_c:
Росіяни просунулися біля Білицького на Донеччині — DeepState
Російські окупанти просунулись в Донецькій області (Фото: www.facebook.com/GeneralStaff.ua)
Російські війська просунулись біля міста Білицьке у Покровському районі Донецької області. Про це у середу, 7 жовтня, повідомив моніторинговий проєкт DeepState.
«Ворог просунувся поблизу Білицького. Уточнено поблизу Котлине», — йдеться у повідомленні.
4 жовтня DeepState повідомляли, що війська РФ окупували Іванівку та просунулися у Новому Шаховому Покровського району Донецької області.
26 вересня 1-й корпус Азов заявив, що місто Добропілля у Донецькій області перебуває під контролем Сил оборони України. Заяви Міністерства оборони країни-агресора Росії про оточення українських військових у населеному пункті не відповідають дійсності.
І село Добропілля, і місто Добропілля розташовані у Покровському районі Донеччини на відстані приблизно сім кілометрів.
Інститут вивчення війни спростував інформацію про оточення Добропілля й оцінив, що найближчі російські позиції розташовані за 10,2 км від міста. Аналітики вважають, що такі російські заяви покликані відвернути увагу від успішної операції Сил оборони в районі Лимана.
Офіцер 12-ї бригади Азов НГУ Даффі в інтерв'ю Radio NV також повідомив, що заяви РФ щодо Добропілля неправдиві.

title: Трамп знову заявив про наближення завершення війни в Україні: що сказав
content_c:
Трамп знову заявив про наближення завершення війни в Україні: що сказав
Президент США Дональд Трамп заявив, що мирне врегулювання війни Росії проти України, за його оцінкою, стає ближчим.
Президент США Дональд Трамп вкотре заявив, що завершення війни в Україні наближається, хоча нинішня ситуація, за його словами, може створювати протилежне враження.
За словами американського президента, мирне врегулювання "насправді стає ближчим".
"Вірте чи ні, але це насправді стає ближче. Хоча так не виглядає", — заявив Трамп.
Водночас він не уточнив, які саме нові обставини чи домовленості дають йому підстави говорити про наближення завершення війни.
Раніше президент Володимир Зеленський після переговорів із Трампом повідомив, що Україна готова до взаємного енергетичного перемир’я за умови, що Росія припинить удари по українській енергетиці, електромережах, системах опалення та водопостачання. За його словами, американська сторона має передати цю пропозицію Москві.
Позиція Росії щодо цієї пропозиції наразі публічно не підтверджена.
description: Президент США Дональд Трамп заявив, що мирне врегулювання війни Росії проти України, за його оцінкою, стає ближчим.

title: Трамп анонсировал разговор с Путиным по поводу чумы в Сибири — AP
content_c:
Президент Соединенных Штатов Дональд Трамп заявил, что позвонит российскому диктатору Владимиру Путину, чтобы обсудить вспышку легочной чумы в сибирском научно-исследовательском институте. Вашингтон обсуждает ситуацию и планирует в ближайшее время обнародовать дополнительную информацию. Об этом сообщило информационное агентство Associated Press.
Президент США сообщил о запланированном звонке 6 октября во время общения с журналистами в Белом доме. По его словам, разговор состоится «очень скоро». Органы здравоохранения выясняют обстоятельства смерти женщины. Российские власти назвали причиной её смерти пневмонию неизвестного происхождения, а возможный случай чумы остаётся предметом проверки.
Журналисты спросили Трампа, какой информацией по этому случаю располагает американская разведка. Он ответил, что США ведут «очень тщательное обсуждение» ситуации. При этом президент не раскрыл его содержания.
«Мы сможем сообщить об этом, вероятно, завтра», — заявил Трамп.
Всемирная организация здравоохранения 6 октября оценила риск за пределами России как «очень низкий». Агентство ООН сообщило, что поддерживает связь с российскими властями. Поводом послужили сообщения о смерти на прошлой неделе женщины, работавшей в Иркутском научно-исследовательском противочумном институте Сибири и Дальнего Востока.
«Это тяжелая болезнь. Знаете, раньше мы могли её контролировать, но почему-то эти микробы стали сильнее и умнее. Они словно армия», — сказал президент США.
Запланированный звонок состоится на фоне приближения срока принятия решения о новых американских санкциях против России. До 18 октября администрация Трампа должна определить, вводить ли ограничения против российских структур и какие именно. Этот срок предусмотрен законом о санкциях против России и Ирана имени Линдси Грэма. Трамп подписал его 18 сентября.
Украина уже предоставила американской администрации и Конгрессу перечень российских компаний, судов и физических лиц, в отношении которых предлагает ввести санкции. Киев хочет, чтобы Вашингтон применил к ним ограничения в рамках этого закона.
Напомним, что государственный секретарь США Марко Рубио 6 октября призвал Россию предоставить больше информации о возможном случае чумы. Он отметил, что Вашингтон не располагает полными данными об обстоятельствах заболевания и смерти сотрудницы лаборатории. По его словам, пока невозможно определить, будет ли ситуация иметь глобальные последствия.
Кроме того, посольство США в Москве 6 октября опубликовало медицинское предупреждение в связи с сообщениями о возможном случае легочной чумы в Иркутской области. Дипломаты заявили, что отслеживают информацию о смерти сотрудницы института, карантине и закрытии больниц. Они напомнили, что возможности оказания помощи американцам в России ограничены, особенно за пределами Москвы.
description: ВООЗ считает угрозу для других стран очень низкой и поддерживает контакты с российскими властями.

title: У США смертельно поранили 12-річну дівчинку - чоловіки сварилися за паркомісце
content_c:
У США смертельно поранили 12-річну дівчинку - чоловіки сварилися за паркомісце
  - Author, Ана Фегай
  - Reporting from, Вашингтон
- Published
- Час прочитання: 2 хв
У Балтіморі на вихідних загинула 12-річна дівчинка. Трагедія, ймовірно, сталася під час суперечки за паркувальні місце, повідомила поліція американського міста.
Хлоя Ішвей опинилася під перехресним вогнем двох чоловіків, які, за даними поліції, скоріш за все, посварилися через паркомісце біля парку, де діти грали в американський футбол.
"Я дуже сумуватиму за своєю дитиною", - сказала мати Хлої в інтерв'ю CBS, американському партнеру ВВС, наступного дня після смертельної стрілянини.
Окрім дівчинки, поранені ще четверо дорослих. Їхній стан стабільний.
Поліція розшукує щонайменше двох підозрюваних, повідомив на пресконференції комісар поліції Балтімора Річард Ворлі. Арештів поки що не було.
"Нам відомо, що між двома боягузами виникла якась суперечка, - сказав Ворлі. - Вони обидва відкрили вогонь один по одному. Під перехресний вогонь потрапила 12-річна дівчинка, яка, ймовірно, прийшла туди подивитися на футбольний матч. Вона загинула від вогнепальних поранень".
Ворлі заявив, що дівчинка не була ціллю стрілянини.
Хлою Ішвей доправили до лікарні, де вона померла. Четверо інших постраждалих отримали поранення, які не становлять загрози для життя, повідомила поліція Балтімора.
"Я хочу справедливості для моєї дитини", - сказала CBS мати Хлої, Крістін Різ.
Рідні розповіли, що 12-річна дівчинка любила танцювати, музику та проводити час із близькими. Її запам'ятають як люблячу доньку й онуку.
"Вона завжди була зі мною, вона була моєю найкращою подругою", - сказала бабуся Хлої, Донна Різ. За її словами, онука неодмінно телефонувала їй "щодня".
"Я сумуватиму за нею", - сказала вона.
Інцидент стався в суботу після 18:00 за місцевим часом.
Правоохоронці продовжують розслідувати стрілянину і закликають усіх свідків повідомити поліції будь-яку інформацію.
Поки що невідомо, скільки саме пострілів пролунало, сказав Ворлі.
"Двоє дорослих чоловіків посварилися - і тепер 12-річної дівчинки немає", - сказав мер Балтімора Брендон Скотт на пресконференції.
"Ми ніколи не повинні опинятися в ситуації, коли змушені говорити щось подібне. Те, що сталося тут сьогодні, - одна з найогидніших речей, які я коли-небудь бачив у своєму житті".
description: Поліція Балтімора заявила, що дівчинка не була ціллю стрілянини, а опинилася під перехресним вогнем.

title: Посольство США в РФ закликало американців в Іркутській області уникати медзакладів через підозру на легеневу чуму
content_c:
Посольство США в Росії повідомило, що стежить за ситуацією в Іркутській області у зв'язку з повідомленнями про підозру на легеневу чуму, яка призвела до смерті людини, та закликало американських громадян у регіоні уникати закладів, де зафіксовано випадки захворювання.
"Посольству США відомо про повідомлення в пресі з Іркутської області щодо підозри на легеневу чуму, яка призвела до смерті особи, а також про пов'язані з цим карантинні заходи та закриття лікарень в Іркутську. Ми продовжуємо уважно стежити за ситуацією", – йдеться в повідомленні на сайті посольства.
У дипмісії наголосили, що можливості уряду США допомогти американцям у Росії обмежені, особливо за межами Москви. Також на співробітників уряду США можуть поширюватися додаткові обмеження на поїздки до окремих регіонів з міркувань безпеки та охорони здоров'я.
Громадянам США в регіоні радять дотримуватися вказівок місцевих органів охорони здоров'я, негайно звертатися по медичну допомогу в разі появи лихоманки чи симптомів з боку дихальних шляхів, а тим, хто відвідував регіон, – стежити за станом здоров'я протягом 14 днів після повернення.
У посольстві нагадали, що рекомендація Держдепартаменту щодо поїздок до Росії залишається на найвищому, четвертому рівні ("Не подорожувати"), а американцям, які перебувають у РФ, радять негайно виїхати.

title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows
content_c:
A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows
- Published
A sharp increase in human activity is having an impact on the way a Himalayan bird lives and communicates, two studies by Indian researchers have found.
The monal, a pheasant native to Himalayan mountain forests, is deeply woven into the region's cultural, folklore and identity. The eye-catching monal - the male has distinctive green, blue and copper feathers - is the state bird of India's Uttarakhand state and the national bird of Nepal, reflecting its cultural significance across the Himalayas.
But studies show that infrastructure development and tourism are squeezing its habitat, while increasing noise is altering how it communicates with potential mates and rivals.
Researchers from Uttarakhand conducted two separate studies over five years which flagged key threats to the bird.
One study found that the birds are forced to move higher in the mountains as their natural habitat in the alpine meadows above the tree line get crowded. The other says the monal is changing its pitch to cut through human noise in a busy valley.
"These two studies give a useful warning for other more vulnerable species - if the monal is forced to change both its voice and its address, how are the more sensitive species responding?" says Vishal Singh, an environmental practitioner working on ecology and climate issues in the Himalayas.
Dr Rajeev Lochan, lead researcher of both studies, told the BBC that they chose to study the monal as the bird has a narrow habitat range - it moves seasonally between the lower montane zone - an ecological belt found on the lower slopes of the mountains - and high-elevation alpine zones. This, he says, makes it a key indicator of ecosystem health in the north-western Himalayas.
"If the species is facing issues on this particular landscape, there might be a chance that the ecological disturbances are affecting other birds too," said Lochan.
The monal, researchers say, can be seen as a stand-in for the health of a fragile Himalayan ecosystem pushed to a tipping point due to unregulated tourism and heavy urbanisation.
While the region has always drawn tourists, trekkers and researchers given its scenic landscape and biodiversity, rapid infrastructure expansion in the past decade has made more places accessible, increasing footfall and disrupting the wildlife. This, coupled with mounting human pressures, suggests that climate change is emerging as another major threat to the region's already vulnerable biodiversity.
"There are a lot of factors at play but at a broader level, the problem is that the economic development of the region is not aligned to its ecological integrity," Singh said.
According to the first study, climate change is projected to continue shrinking and destabilising the Himalayan monal's habitat across the Indian Himalayas through 2100 under multiple climate scenarios.
Currently, the birds are found in alpine meadows, located high in the mountains above the forests, which form some of the Himalayas' most important seasonal grazing and biodiversity-rich habitats.
The researchers modelled how climate change could shift the monal's suitable habitat across the Indian Himalayan region in the states of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh. It was based on the kind of global climate models and emissions scenarios used for assessments by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the UN's climate science unit.
"These birds are now slowly moving upwards in the Himalayas as the snow is melting and vegetation is growing, making the area accessible to them. They are anyway being pushed upwards as their natural habitats in alpine meadows are being encroached upon by humans," Lochan said.
The model assumes that the bird needs the current climate set-up that exists in alpine meadows in the future too, a reasonable but not certain assumption.
The birds' seasonal migration may become increasingly difficult as changes in climate may force them to move to higher elevations on hills, to smaller and fragmented areas. Their population would be scattered in disconnected pockets, which reduces chances of breeding between groups and increases their risks of long-term decline or local extinction, which is already a threat, the study says.
The second study, also conducted by Lochan, Dinesh Kumar Sharma and Anand Kumar, who work at the Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University, focuses on the bird's behavioural changes. They conducted the study in two valleys in Kedarnath Musk Deer Sanctuary in Uttarakhand - at Chopta, a tourist spot with busy traffic and visitors, and the largely quiet Madmaheshwar.
They recorded more than 700 monal calls across both sites using microphones and passive recording devices and then measured pitch, call length and background noise levels for a year from April 2023.
Birds in noisy environments consistently produced calls with significantly higher peak frequencies compared with those in quieter habitats, the study said.
The researchers found subtle changes in the monal's pitch that could be picked up by recording devices but might go unnoticed by the human ear.
"This does not mean that the species has undergone a permanent or evolutionary change in its vocal frequency; rather, our findings suggest behavioural flexibility in response to different acoustic environments," Lochan said.
Compared with the birds in Madmaheshwar valley, the monal in Chopta also produced shorter call durations likely to cut through low-frequency human noise from traffic and tourist footfall.
Bird calls are one of the most sophisticated forms of sound-based communication in the natural world, and significant changes can interfere with, among other things, their mating success.
"When a species must raise its pitch to be heard over tourist traffic, or climb higher as meadows turn crowded, it reveals how human pressure is rewriting the rules of life in the Himalaya," says Anjal Prakash, a public policy professor at FLAME University and contributor to IPCC reports.
Lochan says he and his team consider this a preliminary study and hope to expand the scope and depth of it.
The research comes with the caveat that it is not conclusive on ecological consequences, and more research is needed. But together, the two studies signal broader ecological stress across the Himalayas.
"In listening to the monal, we hear the Himalayas asking for space, silence and care," says Prakash.
description: A sharp increase in human activity is affecting the way the Himalayan monal lives and communicates, studies show.

title: Badenoch's £10bn air defence plan points to growing concern over protecting UK's skies
content_c:
Badenoch's £10bn air defence plan points to growing concern over protecting UK's skies
- Published
America and Israel's war with Iran has shown that even the world's most sophisticated air defences can be overwhelmed by enemy missiles and drones, if fired in significant numbers.
Iran's have broken through the layered air defences of US military bases in the Middle-East causing significant damage.
Russia's war in Ukraine has also exposed the huge challenge of defending their own skies from large-scale attacks.
The government's Strategic Defence Review, published in 2025, explicitly warned of the threats to the UK – including ballistic and cruise missiles and drones – and highlighted the need for the UK to invest more in its air defences.
The Labour government is allocating up to £1bn to address it.
The Conservatives now say they will spend more - £10 bn - over a decade. Both parties agree that the UK needs layers of air defences.
- Tories pledge £10bn for British anti-missile defence system 
  - Published13 hours ago
Currently the country has a number of systems to deal with short and medium-range threats – from drones to cruise missiles. But the armed forces still lack a weapons system to deal with long-range ballistic and hypersonic missiles.
And those don't come cheap. Each interceptor used by the US Patriot missile system costs about $4m (£3m).
Sophisticated air defences that can deal with a range of threats are expensive. The US Army alone wants to increase its budget for both missiles and interceptors by fourfold next year – to $36bn (£27.1bn).
Israel also spends a significant proportion of its $45bn (£33.9bn) annual military budget on air defences.
For the Conservatives there's also a presentation problem. Their original press release mentioned building a new air defence systems that would be "in essence, a British Iron Dome", referencing Israel's elaborate air defence system.
But any comparison of the challenge of defending Britain's skies with Israel's, about 10% the size of the UK, is naive.
Nor is the threat the same. Israel has regularly been targeted by drones and missiles over the past decade. The UK has not.
The Conservatives now suggest the phrase "Iron Dome" was just a shorthand for better air defences. But even the words "Britannia Shield" may be a misnomer.
It would be nigh on impossible for the UK to develop an air-defence system that could defend the whole country with such limited resources.
At best it could afford a system to protect some key strategic sites – including military bases. At present the UK doesn't even have that.
How much money are other countries spending on air defences?
By BBC Verify
Nick Forienza, a defence analyst from Janes, a military think tank, said the money committed by the government to missile defence under the Defence Investment Plan "is only a fraction of what other countries have declared".
He said the Conservatives' plan to invest £10bn "sounds comparable to what other small countries are doing".
He continued: "Not as small as the Netherlands or Belgium, but let's say Germany or Turkey and now the Greeks are working on something called Achilles Shield.
"That's the kind of magnitude [spending £10bn] that would be required for a serious missile defence system."
Germany is leading the European Sky Shield Initiative (ESSI), a 24‑nation effort to jointly procure air and missile defence systems (IRIS‑T, Patriot, Arrow 3).
Berlin has committed roughly €4bn (£3.4bn) for Arrow 3 alone and is also part of a €5.1bn (£4.3bn) plan to share up to 1,000 Patriot GEM‑T interceptors with Romania, Spain and the Netherlands.
In France, budgets show an "Air and Air Defence" spend of about €4.4bn (£3.7bn) in 2026, but this covers all air force air defence activities, not just missile defence.
Poland, which spends more on defence as a share of its economy than the UK, is building an air and missile defence system worth more than PLN 200bn (£39bn) which will be spent over a number of years.
Related topics
  - Published16 October 2024
description: The government and the Conservatives both agree the UK needs better air defences in an increasingly dangerous world.

title: Braid-creator Jonathan Blow on making the 'biggest puzzle game ever'
content_c:
Braid-creator Jonathan Blow on making the 'biggest puzzle game ever'
- Published
For ten years, Jonathan Blow has been working with a small team on what he believes is "the biggest puzzle game ever made".
The American developer is renowned as one of the fathers of the modern indie game movement, creating the genre-defining puzzle-platformer Braid in 2008.
Now, a decade on from his last project, The Witness, The Order of the Sinking Star is due to be released on Thursday - a game with roughly 1,500 puzzles that he estimates could take around 500 hours to complete.
So why make something the majority of players may never get even halfway through, let alone finish?
"Some people decide what to make based on what's practical or what makes business sense," Blow says. "It's never been the way that I think."
"I sort of make bad business decisions in a sense...because I let the design dominate that process. But then because we did that, we always have something unique," he says.
The game's blurb likens itself to a "game design supercollider" - four worlds viewed from overhead, built on the mechanics of four pre-existing free puzzle games from other designers (with their permission to do so).
These ideas are then "smashed together" to create brand-new brainteasers.
For example, one world's mechanics, based on those from the free 2014 game Mirror Isles by Alan Hazelden, sees players use mirror reflections to swap places across islands.
When combined with the system of another free game created by Hazelden, Skipping Stones to Lonely Homes - where players throw stones into water to create paths - brand-new puzzle opportunities suddenly arise.
Risk and reward
Taking a risk on making something more experimental is what appears to ultimately drive Blow, who says that as the industry has grown, the culture for developers has also changed.
"Somewhere along the way...this idea that the best designers were trying to always make new experiences...just sort of got dropped by the wayside," he says.
The outspoken designer is renowned for his frank takes on the industry - previously calling social media games such as Farmville "evil" and World of Warcraft's quest design "unethical".
In December 2025, Hazelden publicly distanced himself from Blow - writing in a post on Bluesky, external that he was "dismissive of diversity efforts" and "pro-MAGA".
Blow, who has not responded to these critiques publicly, tells me he instead decided to "sit down and focus on the games".
"What the players want from developers is good games," he says.
"They don't want us to be arguing, especially with each other, about political stances."
Blow says he is sceptical of AI, which was "not part of the pipeline at all" for Order of the Sinking Star, even though he recognises it as an "advancement" and an "interesting technology".
Of the benefits often cited by those who use the tech, such as increased productivity, he asks: "If you're saying you're ten times as productive and it's been 3 years, you should have been able to do thirty years of work."
"So where's this output of 30 years of work?"
Despite rejecting the tech, Blow says the industry faces an "uncertain time" in how it deals with AI, particularly with newer creators who may rely too heavily on it to code rather than learning the "weird glyphs" themselves.
"A danger is that not many people know how to program in the future," he says.
"And if AI can't really do everything, then the supply of programmers might not be enough to make good stuff."
A new language
Blow's refusal to compromise on any aspect of the Order of the Sinking Star transcends its core design.
The developer decided to make his own programming language, Jai, from scratch.
He then used this, alongside a custom engine, to make the game.
A game's engine is a piece of software that packs everything needed to craft a playable experience - including graphics rendering, physics simulation and scripting - into one place for creators.
Some developers turn to pre-built game engines such as Unity or Unreal Engine, rather than taking on the considerable challenge of building an engine from scratch.
For Blow, creating his own engine in this language meant he could build something "tuned and authored very specifically" to what he wanted to make.
It is yet another reason he gives for why this project, which started as a simple "design experiment", has taken ten years to finish.
"I do want the next project after this to be less on hard mode, or really it was nightmare mode, because we did so many things on hard mode at the same time," he reflects.
"But it's also been rewarding in a certain way. Because otherwise, what else are you in the industry for?"

title: Outcry in Trinidad and Tobago after passing of police bill that could threaten press freedom
content_c:
Journalists in Trinidad and Tobago have called for an urgent amendment to a sweeping new bill that increases police powers of search and seizure, which they argue threatens the country’s much-vaunted freedom of the press.
The government says the special operations bill 2026, passed on 24 September, is designed to tackle alarmingly high crime and murder rates in the Caribbean nation.
The country has spent more than a year in an almost perpetual state of emergency, with police empowered to bypass normal constitutional rights around arrest, detention, and search and seizure.
But journalists in Trinidad and Tobago have called for explicit exemptions in the new legislation to prevent police from searching and seizing their notebooks, phones and laptops.
In the past, journalists have been forced to challenge warrants empowering police to raid their homes and offices.
Although the country prides itself in honouring freedom of speech, ranking 19 out of 180 countries in the 2025 Reporters Without Borders press freedom index, this year it fell 13 places to 32, and journalists say they are deeply concerned about whether they can protect whistleblowers and vulnerable sources who share information on the understanding that they will be protected.
The president of the Media Association of Trinidad and Tobago (MATT), Prior Beharry, said the organisation had called for clause 15 of the bill to be urgently amended “to explicitly shield our devices and materials … and confidential source information from standard police seizure”.
Clause 15 prevents police from seizing “a tool of a lawful trade or business” or material protected by legal professional privilege. But MATT says journalism is not explicitly recognised as a protected trade, nor does the bill establish a procedure for handling confidential journalistic material discovered during searches. It wants the clause changed to “expressly name journalism as a protected lawful trade and safeguard journalists’ devices, materials and confidential sources”.
Beharry said the bill’s search‑and‑seizure powers were particularly worrying in a digital era where “the tools of a journalist is … usually [a] cell phone”. Though he said journalists had not been directly threatened under recent states of emergency, he warned that other restrictions were worsening.
“One of the issues we are having is the access to the government, the executive, including the prime minister, who has not had an official press conference for more than a year,” he said. “Ministries use state resources and we are not invited, but state media is invited.”
The independent journalist Pearce Robinson said the combination of surveillance capability, expanded search powers – without explicit protection for journalistic practice – and declining access to government ministers created a “concrete” threat to press freedom, with a particularly significant impact on investigative reporting.
“If your phone, your laptop and your notes can be searched or seized without explicit protection for journalistic material, that raises serious constitutional concerns,” he said. “Investigative journalism depends on people being able to speak confidentially.”
He also raised concerns about phone tapping and surveillance, pointing to an investigation by the Trinidad and Tobago Guardian which said that “judges approved 314 warrants to intercept communications in Trinidad and Tobago between 2020 and May 2026”.
“My concern is not that press freedom has disappeared,” he said. “It is that several of these pressures … are accumulating at the same time.”
Pedro Cárdenas, of the press freedom and human rights organisation Article 19, expressed concern about the clause in the new bill. “It empowers law enforcement officers to seize any vehicle, article or document deemed likely to be of substantial value. We find this clause particularly problematic because it is vague and opens up to discussion what is substantial value or not,” he said.
He added that it “might directly counter” existing international human rights laws.
The office of the prime minister did not respond to a request for comment.
Stuart Young, Trinidad and Tobago’s former prime minister, labelled the bill “unconstitutional and very dangerous”, adding that it “breaches fundamental and entrenched constitutional rights” and was passed “without a required constitutional majority in highly questionable circumstances”.
He said the government’s past use of emergency powers – including detaining citizens without charge – showed “the real likelihood of abuse” under the new legislation.
author: Natricia Duncan Caribbean correspondent

title: Kemi Badenoch is the most rightwing leader in Tory history. Isn’t it time she got some actual scrutiny? | Owen Jones
content_c:
The Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, will march on to the conference stage in Birmingham feeling buoyed. “Kemi’s soaring,” coos the Sun, and that sums up the prevailing wisdom. More than four in 10 Britons think she is doing well as Tory leader, compared with a third who think otherwise. As Nigel Farage’s stock has plummeted thanks to scandals over a £5m personal gift and donations from crypto billionaires, the polling suggests that the Conservatives could regain the mantle of Britain’s main rightwing force.
Yet Badenoch has been the beneficiary of circumstance. Her tenure as opposition leader has been defined by Keir Starmer’s project imploding almost as soon as it gained power. When Reform UK enjoyed its seismic polling lead, the Tory plight was double-edged: they were starved of attention, but that inevitably resulted in a lack of scrutiny, too. It has been easy for Badenoch to appear formidable while her opponents have disintegrated.
With the Conservatives now back in the race, the spotlight falls on Badenoch. Let us consider the absurdity of her proposed air defence system. Our would-be prime minister denied comparing it to Israel’s Iron Dome, despite the term appearing in both a press release and a newspaper article under her own name. This amateurishness is one thing, but even on its own terms, her proposal is a mess. It will “protect the whole United Kingdom, our sovereign territories and British bases overseas”, she claims, which would be impossible for the £10bn over 10 years she is proposing to spend on it. The former British general Richard Barrons suggests such a system would cost more than £100bn.
What does this say about Badenoch’s sense of priorities? The actual urgent national security threat Britain faces is not volleys of missile attacks, but the climate emergency. There were estimated to be thousands of excess deaths from heatwaves this summer, while our intelligence services warn of serious disruption to our food supply from 2030. Yet Badenoch has committed to repealing the Climate Change Act and claimed that net zero by 2050 is “impossible” without bankrupting Britain. This not only contradicts the conclusion of the government’s statutory climate scientific advisers, but Badenoch herself. As a Treasury minister in 2021, she told parliament that it would cost less than 2% of GDP, largely from “increased investment in growth markets of the future”. Even three former Tory prime ministers have criticised Badenoch’s shift against net zero – including the former rightwing pin-up Boris Johnson.
Then there’s her economic agenda. A year ago, Badenoch declared that she sought to become Britain’s version of Argentina’s far-right president, Javier Milei. His government has imposed devastating cuts to pensions, universities and public healthcare, while poverty is once more surging. Badenoch proposes welfare cuts worth £23bn, and misleads the public as she does so. In May, she declared: “For the first time ever, the total welfare bill is now higher than total receipts from income tax.” This has been the case since 2011, and as the UK Statistics Authority noted in a letter rebuking her, this was misleading for other reasons: the gap had actually narrowed in recent years, and most of the welfare bill goes to pensioner benefits, including the state pension.
What would £23bn in cuts mean? They would include stripping workers with indefinite leave to remain of social security – people who have lived here for years, worked and paid taxes. That would not only be an injustice to them – consider that there is already a staffing crisis in sectors such as social care that immigration restrictions are worsening. She would reinstate a two-child benefit cap that would drive hundreds of thousands of children into poverty. Most of the rest would fall on the shoulders of sick and disabled people, including those receiving support while they work.
Consider this too: while we still live with the consequences of the 2008 financial crash, Badenoch proposes ending the ringfence for big banks separating retail and investment activities, and reducing their capital requirements.
What of her authoritarianism? Badenoch has declared free speech to be “the birthright of every citizen”, yet has advocated a blanket ban on pro-Palestinian protests. The justification is conflating opposition to genocide with threats to Jewish people, but this is a Tory leader who, when asked about Gaza, said that “Israel is fighting a proxy war on behalf of the UK”. Withdrawal from the European convention on human rights and repealing the Human Rights Act would strip citizens of crucial protections against an overbearing executive and abuses of state power. Badenoch advocates an ICE-style mass deportation apparatus with sweeping powers of surveillance – directly mimicking an institution across the Atlantic that snatches people from the street and kills migrants and US citizens alike.
Her attitude to the rights of minorities, meanwhile, is underlined by her commitment to scrap the public sector equality duty in its entirety. As a minister in 2021, she backed it, saying it helped ensure “that fairness is at the heart of everything we do”.
Yet the average punter knows little about Badenoch. The increasing extremism and scandals of Farageism have allowed her to appear somehow more reasonable and stable in comparison. But Badenoch is easily the most rightwing Tory leader in the party’s history. Her programme is a wishlist of rightwing zealots – one which would be ruinous to our social fabric. Yet few have bothered to look under the bonnet. The danger is that Britain discovers what Badenoch really stands for only when she is close enough to power to put it into practice.
- 
  Owen Jones is a Guardian columnist
